criteria.text: The current and intended Clipboard owner, caller, dependency direction, mutable-state writer, lifetime owner, XAML contract, and shortest reading route are documented from source.
RecipeCommandSurface contains no direct System.Windows.Clipboard calls; Shell owns the actual WPF Clipboard callback while Surface retains command/status behavior.
Focused injected callback copy/paste contracts and the required Debug build pass; actual desktop clipboard, WPF theme/DPI/monitor/input, hardware, and long-running native limits are explicit.
Handoff and codebase navigation record the new boundary, preserved public/XAML contracts, first-contributor effect, changed files, and remaining RecipeCommandSurface debt.

artifacts.summary: Focused evidence for the RecipeCommandSurface WPF Clipboard boundary.

evidence.observation: The source audit records five direct System.Windows.Clipboard calls in RecipeCommandSurface: four SetText handlers and one ContainsText/GetText paste handler. The owner map records the before/after call path, mutable-state writer, Shell composition/lifetime owner, protected XAML command/status/XML contract, and the exact reason this external system boundary is independent. The source inventory and scope decision are stored in owner-map.txt, clipboard-inventory.txt, composition-call-sites.txt, and scope-decision.txt.

RecipeCommandSurface receives copyTextToClipboard, clipboardContainsText, and readClipboardText callbacks; all five direct Surface Clipboard calls were replaced. OpenVisionShellHostView supplies System.Windows.Clipboard callbacks. source-proof.txt, surface-clipboard-search.txt, callback-call-path.txt, and git-diff.txt record the changed dependency direction and absence of a new abstraction layer.

Solution Debug and VisionRecipeRunnerSmoke x64 Debug builds passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. The copied-runtime PL-0024 callback contract passed 3/3; RefreshOptions passed 1/1; Validation Set success passed 1/1; Validation Set error passed 1/1; Shell Recipe basic lifecycle passed 7/7. The summary and build logs are in m3-focused; actual desktop Clipboard and full WPF/device/long-run matrices remain unverified.

The final audit records Surface/Shell owners, callback dependency direction, mutable-state and lifetime owners, preserved XAML commands and status/XML contracts, the nested Commands navigation region, no new partial or folder, and the remaining broad Surface debt. Final solution and Smoke Debug builds passed with 0 warnings/errors; the copied-runtime callback contract passed 3/3; documentation index, RefactorAudit, readiness, diff, and issue-ledger checks passed. Actual desktop Clipboard and full WPF/device/long-run runtime boundaries remain unverified.

events.summary: Move only System.Windows.Clipboard side effects to narrow callbacks supplied by the existing OpenVisionShellHostView composition owner. Keep RecipeCommandSurface command, status, and XML state ownership; add no interface, manager, wrapper, or partial.

Use the existing Shell composition boundary with three optional concrete callbacks instead of adding a Clipboard interface or wrapper. This keeps the production WPF side effect in OpenVisionShellHostView and preserves source compatibility for existing test callers.

Keep the callback-only Clipboard boundary after the copied-runtime contract and existing Recipe regression contracts passed. No desktop Clipboard automation or additional abstraction is required for this source boundary.

Close this Clipboard boundary: the external WPF side effect is owned by the existing Shell composition owner, the Surface retains protected command/status/XML contracts, the Commands region is navigation-only, and no further file-length split is justified by this evidence.

PL-0024 resolved: WPF Clipboard access was moved from RecipeCommandSurface to existing Shell composition callbacks, focused contracts and Debug builds passed, and the final owner/MVVM/command-binding/partial/folder/navigation audit is recorded. The remaining broad Surface regions require a new proven boundary before reopening.
